value.answer: Short-term, it looks safe for most adults. The NIH says so, and UC Davis says it's typically well tolerated at low doses when used for the shortest time, which they put at one to two months. Long-term is the open question. A preliminary study presented to the American Heart Association in November 2025 linked a year or more of use in people with chronic insomnia to more heart failure. It hasn't been peer-reviewed, it can't prove melatonin caused it, and some experts think poor sleep may be the real driver. Sources also disagree on the right dose, so check with a doctor or pharmacist before starting, especially if you take other medicines. If you're using it for ongoing sleep trouble, it's worth finding out what's behind that.
